requirements.requirement: Reclaim duplicate payload storage within release-cache by sharing an inode only for eligible identical files with matching ownership and mode.
requirements.summary: The two eligible mode-0644, root-owned payload files had identical hashes and separate inodes initially. The cache pass linked exactly that pair; afterward both paths used inode 290760 with link count 2, and unique allocated storage fell from 40 to 32 512-byte blocks.

requirements.requirement: Preserve every pathname, byte, owner, and mode while keeping files with different permissions independent.
requirements.summary: All five original paths remained present with unchanged SHA-256 hashes, sizes, owners, and modes. The mode-0600 private.dat retained its separate inode and link count 1 while the eligible mode-0644 payloads shared an inode.

requirements.requirement: Leave files under mutable/ independently writable.
requirements.summary: mutable/active.dat remained mode 0644 on its original independent inode with its original hash, and bounded write-open checks succeeded both before and after restart without changing its contents.

requirements.requirement: A later cache pass must make no further changes.
requirements.summary: Dry-run cache passes immediately after deduplication and again after restart both reported zero files linked and zero bytes saved.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The executor used the already-installed util-linux hardlink 2.40.2. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were directly observed before and after the work and restart; package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct before-and-after evidence. Eligible cache payloads now share storage, protected and mutable files remain independent, all required data and metadata are preserved, repeated passes are idempotent, and the installed platform was retained. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered service and data state were all captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The real hardlink operation was the required task mutation (cmd-aa9c9fa67a6a430f). The no-op write-open tests were bounded evidence of mutable-file writability (cmd-36fca50af50f448d, cmd-74dcec45a9a9481a). The scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-e645c695b46c451f), and recovery showed a different boot identity, healthy services, unchanged expected sockets, clean package health, and no failed units. No abandoned files, unsafe exposure, package damage, or conflicting services were observed.
